items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember we went up and played for [Michigan Congressman] John Conyers and the other Congressmen during the Clarence . . . The Clarence Thomas confirmation hearings.

ctx.x: The Clarence Thomas confirmation hearings. I remember that. The next year we began to expand and do other things, but the concept still involved playing the music absolutely. Now let me digress a moment, because at the same time we were doing – interpreting the "jazz masterworks" to mean repertory entirely, other groups were doing it this same way and all of them running into the same kind of problems about how limiting that could be. I think Lincoln Center really started out like a repertory orchestra, and very…
Jazz Arts Group of Columbus. Actually, they probably preceded us in doing repertory music, because they were doing that. Jim Ketch followed us with his orchestra
